prompt:
**(a)** Find a vector equation of the line through $A(1,2,-1)$ and $B(3,-1,2)$. **[2]**

**(b)** Determine whether $C(7,-7,8)$ lies on the line. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Direction $\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\3\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)**; $\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-1\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\3\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $\lambda=3$ gives $(7,-7,8)$ in all three components, so yes **(A1)**

prompt: In the vector equation $\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b$, state what $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\lambda$ represent.
markscheme: $\mathbf a$: position vector of a known point on the line; $\mathbf b$: a direction vector of the line; $\lambda$: a scalar parameter — each real value gives one point on the line **(A1)**

prompt: Find the acute angle between the lines $\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}0\\3\\1\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}$.

A ship's position $t$ hours after noon is $\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\end{pmatrix}+t\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}$ km, where $\mathbf i$ is east and $\mathbf j$ is north.

**(a)** Find the speed of the ship. **[1]**

**(b)** Find the time and position when the ship is due east of the origin. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\left|\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}\right|=5\ \text{km h}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Due east of $O$: north component $0$: $-3+3t=0$ **(M1)**, $t=1$ (13:00) **(A1)**; position $(6,0)$ **(A1)**
